title: Human Genome Project
summary: An international research effort to read all human DNA, launched in October 1990. In the United States the National Institutes of Health and the Department of Energy ran it. A working draft was announced on 26 June 2000, and on 14 April 2003 the International Human Genome Sequencing Consortium announced completion, more than two years ahead of schedule.

uncertainty.note: Start is the official beginning on 1 October 1990; end is the completion announcement of 14 April 2003.

where.historical_name: National Center for Human Genome Research, National Institutes of Health, Bethesda, Maryland, United States

importance.justification: Produced the reference sequence of the human genome and set open-data norms for genomics.

beats.caption: The Human Genome Project officially begins as an international effort led in the US by NIH and the Department of Energy.
The international consortium announces a working draft of the human genome sequence.
Completion is announced, more than two years ahead of schedule, finishing the project's sequencing goal.

reviewer_note: Pinned at Bethesda as the US NIH lead; the project was international and several non-US centres did much of the sequencing, which I did not source. The 2003 completion covered the gene-containing sequence, not every base.
